summary:
"Exploring Mars isn't just about distance; it's about survival.

That is why we built RedWay. Under the hood, we transform heavy NASA satellite imagery into persistent polygons in our database, and with that we apply differential calculus for slope estimation, among others.

This data feeds our A-Star algorithm to generate safe routes, evaluating obstacles, radiation, and terrain relief. Through real-time layer rendering and our physical scale model, you can visually experience how we merge engineering with art.

With RedWay, we aren't just mapping... we are ensuring our rovers endure Mars."
details:
RedWay is a web-based tactical viewer designed for planning rover traverses on the surface of Mars, specifically within the Jezero crater. It combines a high-resolution digital elevation model (DEM) with terrain analysis to display—on an interactive map—hazardous zones, areas offering protection from radiation, and the optimal path between two points.

2. The Problem

• Mobility: Rovers have slope limitations (set at 15° for this project) and can become immobilized by rocks exceeding ~1 meter in height.

• Radiation: The Martian surface is exposed to cosmic rays, lacking the protection of a dense atmosphere or a global magnetic field. Certain terrain features—such as the bases of escarpments or deep canyons—can obstruct parts of the sky, thereby reducing radiation exposure.

• Scale: The operational area spans ~21 × 21 km at a 1-meter resolution, comprising over 450 million elevation data points—a scale that cannot be analyzed by eye. Our proposal: process the terrain data once (identifying slopes, rocks, and potential shelters), store it in a geospatial database, and provide a map that can be explored fluidly, along with a route planner that accounts for both obstacles and shelters.

Main Sources:

HiRISE Digital Terrain Model (DTM) of the Jezero crater (JEZ_hirise_soc_006_DTM_..._1m_Eqc...tif): 21,400 × 21,488 pixels at 1-meter resolution, ~1.7 GB, using an equirectangular projection for Mars (+proj=eqc +R=3396190). Jezero is the landing site for NASA’s Perseverance rover (2021).
